<new_user@email.msn.com> writes:

> Ph.D. Ted Kaczynski writes:
> 
> "..In the United States, a couple of decades ago when leftists were a
> minority in our universities, leftist professors were vigorous proponents of
> academic freedom, but today, in those universities where leftists have
> become dominant, they have shown themselves ready to take away from everyone
> else's academic freedom. (This is 'political correctness.)'  [216]
> 
> "Today, in those of our universities where 'political correctness' has
> become dominant, there are probably many leftish types who privately
> disapprove of the suppression of academic freedom, but they go along with it
> anyway." [225]
> 
> 
> Now, if we get rid of our preconceived notions and biases with regard to
> Ted, we will see that much of his views sound very familiar with how other
> adacemics and scholars feel.   While it has been implied that his Manifesto
> gives evidence of his "paranoia", the truth is that no one would even
> suspect him to be mentally unstable if he had not been caught; in other
> words, it's only after the fact that people say, "look at his Manifesto and
> you'll see that he is warped."

I agree that a reader of the Manifesto would be surprised to learn
that the author was a serial killer.  The reader would also not
conclude that the author was psychotic - unless he disagreed strongly
and was in the habit of regarding people he disagreed with as
psychotic.  He also would not regard the author as being of low
intelligence unless this was his general view of people he disagreed
with.

The two quoted paragraphs correspond to my observations.

The first point has been stated many times as New User's further
quotes indicate.  The second is less often said but also not unique.
I'm not complaining about TK saying what others have also said.

One of the characteristics of high IQ is the ability to keep different
points of view separate.  A stupid person might have left some hint
that he likes to kill barking dogs in the Manifesto.

It seems to me that hardly anyone would regard the Manifesto as an
incitement to kill people.
